Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION

This lesson covers The Conquest of Makkah (Fat-hul Makkah) • The Battle of Hunayn, part of History of Islam in Grade 6 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to a story /watch a video/film on fat-hul Makkah and make a presentation on the events,

3. discuss the reasons that led to the battle of Hunayn and make class presentation,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to a story /watch a video/film on fat-hul Makkah and make a presentation on the events,
2. discuss the lessons learnt from the events of fat-hul Makkah and display on charts (e.g. forgiveness, purity of places of worship, love of one’s enemies as an effective daawa, Islam stands for peace),
3. discuss the reasons that led to the battle of Hunayn and make class presentation,
4. discuss the effects of the battle of Hunayn and write notes,
5. dramatise acts depicting peaceful ways of 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on The Conquest of Makkah (Fat-hul Makkah) • The Battle of Hunayn together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: interacting with digital technology enhanced as learners search/watch videos on victory over Makkah.

• Communication and Collaboration: listening, speaking, writing and teamwork skills achieved through group discussions,

presentations and listening to narrations on fat-hul Makkah.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: explanation skills enhanced as learners discuss the lessons learnt from the conquest

of Makkah and their relevance in today’s life.

Values:
• Peace: compassion and care as learners discuss lessons learnt from the events of fat-hul Makkah.

• Respect: acceptance as learners discuss lessons learnt from the events of fat-hul Makkah.
